correctness.rationale: For 1<p<2 and equal-strength rank-one A=a x*, B=b y*, Gram factorization gives denominator eigenvalues 1±c and numerator squared singular-value product (1-c²)(1-d²), trace bounded by 2+2cd. Because p/2 lies in (1/2,1), maximizing phase and then strictly concave output overlap yields d=tanh((p/(2-p))atanh(c)). The remaining derivative equation tanh u+tanh(gamma u)=2tanh(pu) has one positive root by the monotone hyperbolic auxiliary ratio, with endpoints quotient 1. Implicit-root expansion yields kappa(p-1)^2-kappa(p-1)^3. I independently bracketed all positive derivative zeroes over 0.001..10 for p=1.05,1.2,1.5,1.9 and computed maximizing constants 1.000522932,1.007324966,1.036414357,1.08692083, consistent with unique interior maximizer. Finite scanning does not establish uniqueness; source monotonicity proof does.
